Stylized Kelp GPU

Visit Unity Asset Store
    { "Core Concepts": { "entries": { "⚙️ Kelp Settings": { "id": "Core-Concepts/Kelp-Settings", "title": "⚙️ Kelp Settings", "order": 1, "content": "<p><img src=\"cachedImage-../images/kelp-settings-banner.png\" alt=\"\"></p>\n<h1 id=\"Kelp-Settings\" tabindex=\"-1\">Kelp Settings</h1>\n<p>Each kelp instance has a kelp setting assigned. This kelp setting dictates how the kelp is rendered in the scene and influences many aspects such as color, leaf size, and many more properties (see below):</p>\n<p>Kelp settings are stored as ScriptableObjects and can be created by clicking <code>Create</code> &gt; <code>Stylized Kelp</code> &gt; <code>Kelp Settings</code>. From there you can customize the kelp to your liking. <strong>Many properties can be updated at runtime,</strong> so make sure to hit play and then start adjusting:</p>\n<p><img src=\"cachedImage-../images/kelp-settings.png\" alt=\"Kelp Settings Inspector\"></p>\n<p>Some additional settings can also be found on the <code>Stylized Kelp Renderer</code> component, such as wind settings and quality settings (see next section for more details).</p>\n<h1 id=\"Customizable-Properties\" tabindex=\"-1\">Customizable Properties</h1>\n<p>Below you can find an overview of all customizable properties within a kelp setting. This might be overwhelming at first but don't worry, start with the color settings and leaf/stem size and then explore the other settings as you go along!</p>\n<h3 id=\"Stem-Settings\" tabindex=\"-1\">Stem Settings</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Setting</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>Stem Color</code></td>\n<td>The color that is uniformly applied to the stem.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>Stem Segment Length</code></td>\n<td>The length of each stem segment.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>Stem Gravity</code></td>\n<td>The gravity that is applied to the stem. Greater values will cause a higher righting force on the stem itself, whereas lower values will cause the kelp to take longer to straighten out again.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3 id=\"Leaf-Settings\" tabindex=\"-1\">Leaf Settings</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Setting</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>Leaf Start Color</code></td>\n<td>The color that is applied to the leaf at its root.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>Leaf Tip Color</code></td>\n<td>The tip color of the leaf.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>Leaves per Stem Segment</code></td>\n<td>Number of leaves that will be spawned for each stem segment.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>Leaf Length</code></td>\n<td>The length of the leaves.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>Leaf Width</code></td>\n<td>The width of the leaves.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>Randomize Leaf Rotation</code></td>\n<td>Should the leaf rotation be randomized or uniform using the &quot;Leaf Windings&quot; setting?</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>Leaf Windings</code></td>\n<td>Only takes effect, if Randomize Leaf Rotation is false. How many rotations/laps around the stem should the leaves take for each segment?</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>Leaf Rightening Force</code></td>\n<td>The righting force applied to the leaves. Higher values cause flatter leaves</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>Leaf Gravity</code></td>\n<td>The gravity that is applied to the leaves themselves, causing them to either hang downwards or upwards.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>Leaf Tip Gravity Multiplier</code></td>\n<td>The gravity multiplier that is applied to the tip of the leaf, allowing you to modify the behaviour of leaf tips (to i.e. ensure they point upwards).</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2 id=\"Examples\" tabindex=\"-1\">Examples</h2>\n<p>The below examples showcase how some of the settings affect the overall look and behavior of the kelp.</p>\n<p><img src=\"cachedImage-../images/leaf-gravity-example.png\" alt=\"Leaf Gravity Example\">\nLeaf gravity allows you to control how the leaves behave in the scene. Positive values cause the leaves to hang upwards, whereas negative values cause the leaves to point downwards.</p>\n<p><img src=\"cachedImage-../images/leaf-tip-gravity-example.png\" alt=\"Leaf Tip Gravity Example\">\nThe leaf tip gravity allows you to further customize the behaviour of the leaf tips - you can use this to bend the tips of the leaves either upwards or downwards.</p>\n<p><img src=\"cachedImage-../images/leaf-color-example.png\" alt=\"Leaf Color Example\">\nThe leaf colors can be customized using the start and tip color settings. This allows you to create a gradient effect on the leaves. This also supports HDR colors, allowing you to create glowing leaves!</p>\n", "textContent": "Kelp Settings\r\n\r\nEach kelp instance has a kelp setting assigned. This kelp setting dictates how the kelp is rendered in the scene and influences many aspects such as color, leaf size, and many more properties (see below):\r\n\r\nKelp settings are stored as ScriptableObjects and can be created by clicking Create > Stylized Kelp > Kelp Settings. From there you can customize the kelp to your liking. Many properties can be updated at runtime, so make sure to hit play and then start adjusting:\r\n\r\nKelp Settings Inspector\r\n\r\nSome additional settings can also be found on the Stylized Kelp Renderer component, such as wind settings and quality settings (see next section for more details).\r\nCustomizable Properties\r\n\r\nBelow you can find an overview of all customizable properties within a kelp setting. This might be overwhelming at first but don't worry, start with the color settings and leaf/stem size and then explore the other settings as you go along!\r\nStem Settings\r\n\r\n| Setting | Description |\r\n| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\r\n| Stem Color | The color that is uniformly applied to the stem. |\r\n| Stem Segment Length | The length of each stem segment. |\r\n| Stem Gravity | The gravity that is applied to the stem. Greater values will cause a higher righting force on the stem itself, whereas lower values will cause the kelp to take longer to straighten out again. |\r\nLeaf Settings\r\n\r\n| Setting | Description |\r\n| ----------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\r\n| Leaf Start Color | The color that is applied to the leaf at its root. |\r\n| Leaf Tip Color | The tip color of the leaf. |\r\n| Leaves per Stem Segment | Number of leaves that will be spawned for each stem segment. |\r\n| Leaf Length | The length of the leaves. |\r\n| Leaf Width | The width of the leaves. |\r\n| Randomize Leaf Rotation | Should the leaf rotation be randomized or uniform using the \"Leaf Windings\" setting? |\r\n| Leaf Windings | Only takes effect, if Randomize Leaf Rotation is false. How many rotations/laps around the stem should the leaves take for each segment? |\r\n| Leaf Rightening Force | The righting force applied to the leaves. Higher values cause flatter leaves |\r\n| Leaf Gravity | The gravity that is applied to the leaves themselves, causing them to either hang downwards or upwards. |\r\n| Leaf Tip Gravity Multiplier | The gravity multiplier that is applied to the tip of the leaf, allowing you to modify the behaviour of leaf tips (to i.e. ensure they point upwards). |\r\nExamples\r\n\r\nThe below examples showcase how some of the settings affect the overall look and behavior of the kelp.\r\n\r\nLeaf Gravity Example\r\nLeaf gravity allows you to control how the leaves behave in the scene. Positive values cause the leaves to hang upwards, whereas negative values cause the leaves to point downwards.\r\n\r\nLeaf Tip Gravity Example\r\nThe leaf tip gravity allows you to further customize the behaviour of the leaf tips - you can use this to bend the tips of the leaves either upwards or downwards.\r\n\r\nLeaf Color Example\r\nThe leaf colors can be customized using the start and tip color settings. This allows you to create a gradient effect on the leaves. This also supports HDR colors, allowing you to create glowing leaves!", "wordCount": 556, "readingTime": 3, "isPage": true }, "🎥 Stylized Kelp Renderer": { "id": "Core-Concepts/Stylized-Kelp-Renderer", "title": "🎥 Stylized Kelp Renderer", "order": 2, "content": "<p><img src=\"cachedImage-../images/kelp-renderer-banner.png\" alt=\"\"></p>\n<h1 id=\"Stylized-Kelp-Renderer\" tabindex=\"-1\">Stylized Kelp Renderer</h1>\n<p>The stylized kelp renderer is the main point of interaction for the stylized kelp asset. It is responsible for rendering the kelp in your scene and provides many options to customize the look and feel of the kelp.</p>\n<p>The kelp renderer <strong>can be enabled/disabled at runtime</strong> to save on performance when the kelp is not visible. Additionally, if required, it is possible to have multiple kelp renderers in your scene, each rendering different sections of your level.</p>\n<h3 id=\"General-Settings\" tabindex=\"-1\">General Settings</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Setting</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>Self Initialize</code></td>\n<td>Should the kelp renderer self initialize itself? If yes, it will do so in OnEnable, preventing any additions of kelp afterwards. If disabled, you need to call Initialize() yourself.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3 id=\"Wind-Settings\" tabindex=\"-1\">Wind Settings</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Setting</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>Wind Strength</code></td>\n<td>The strength of the wind.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>Wind Speed</code></td>\n<td>The speed of the wind.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>Wind Scale</code></td>\n<td>A wind strength multiplier per direction. Allows you to reduce the wind i.e. in the up/down direction.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3 id=\"Subsurface-Scattering-Settings\" tabindex=\"-1\">Subsurface Scattering Settings</h3>\n<p>The kelp supports a subsurface scattering effect for the main directional light in the scene. This effect boosts the color, when the directional light is shining through the kelp. This effect is only visible when the light is behind the kelp, relative to the camera.</p>\n<p><img src=\"cachedImage-../images/subsurface-scattering-banner.png\" alt=\"\"></p>\n<p>You can control the strength of the effect with the settings below.</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Setting</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>Scattering Color Boost</code></td>\n<td>How much to boost the color, when the main light shines through the kelp. 1 is equivalent to no boost.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>Scattering Amount</code></td>\n<td>The amount of light scattered by the kelp.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3 id=\"Simulation-Settings\" tabindex=\"-1\">Simulation Settings</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Setting</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>Stem Constraint Iterations</code></td>\n<td>The number of stem segment constraint iterations per frame. Higher values result in a more accurate simulation, but increase performance cost. Try to use a low value if possible.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>Leaf Constraint Iterations</code></td>\n<td>The number of leaf segment constraint iterations per frame. Higher values result in a more accurate simulation, but increase performance cost. Try to use a low value if possible.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>Damping Factor</code></td>\n<td>How much of the movement is retained per constraint iteration. Lower values result in a more stiff kelp, whereas higher values result in a more floaty kelp.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>Update Mode</code></td>\n<td>The used update mode for the kelp simulation. See <a href=\"#Performance/Update-Mode\">Update Mode</a></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>Skip Updates</code></td>\n<td>The updates to skip, before the next update is scheduled. See <a href=\"#Performance/Update-Mode\">Update Mode</a></td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3 id=\"Collision-Settings\" tabindex=\"-1\">Collision Settings</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Setting</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>Enable Collision</code></td>\n<td>Should collision be enabled for the kelp? Enabling collision allows the kelp to collide with any collider in the scene, but comes at a performance cost, especially for complex scenes or large amounts of kelp. The collision is calculated per stem segment on the CPU.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>Collision Mask</code></td>\n<td>The layermask used for collisions with the environment.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>Segment Collision Radius</code></td>\n<td>The radius of the collision sphere per stem segment that is used to approximate the collisions of the kelp stem with its environments.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3 id=\"Performance-Settings\" tabindex=\"-1\">Performance Settings</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Setting</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>Simulation Distance</code></td>\n<td>The distance from the camera at which kelp instances will be simulated. Setting this to a lower value can help with performance.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>Player Transform</code></td>\n<td>The transform of the player/main camera. Kelp instances will be simulated based on the player's position. If left empty, the Camera.main will be used.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n", "textContent": "Stylized Kelp Renderer\r\nThe stylized kelp renderer is the main point of interaction for the stylized kelp asset. It is responsible for rendering the kelp in your scene and provides many options to customize the look and feel of the kelp.\r\n\r\nThe kelp renderer can be enabled/disabled at runtime to save on performance when the kelp is not visible. Additionally, if required, it is possible to have multiple kelp renderers in your scene, each rendering different sections of your level.\r\nGeneral Settings\r\n\r\n| Setting \t| Description \t|\r\n|---------------\t|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\t|\r\n| Self Initialize \t| Should the kelp renderer self initialize itself? If yes, it will do so in OnEnable, preventing any additions of kelp afterwards. If disabled, you need to call Initialize() yourself. \t|\r\nWind Settings\r\n\r\n| Setting \t| Description \t|\r\n|---------------\t|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\t|\r\n| Wind Strength \t| The strength of the wind. \t|\r\n| Wind Speed \t| The speed of the wind. \t|\r\n| Wind Scale \t| A wind strength multiplier per direction. Allows you to reduce the wind i.e. in the up/down direction. \t|\r\nSubsurface Scattering Settings\r\nThe kelp supports a subsurface scattering effect for the main directional light in the scene. This effect boosts the color, when the directional light is shining through the kelp. This effect is only visible when the light is behind the kelp, relative to the camera. \r\n\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\nYou can control the strength of the effect with the settings below.\r\n\r\n| Setting \t| Description \t|\r\n|---------------\t|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\t|\r\n| Scattering Color Boost \t| How much to boost the color, when the main light shines through the kelp. 1 is equivalent to no boost. \t|\r\n| Scattering Amount \t| The amount of light scattered by the kelp. \t|\r\nSimulation Settings\r\n| Setting \t| Description \t|\r\n|-------------------\t|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\t|\r\n| Stem Constraint Iterations \t| The number of stem segment constraint iterations per frame. Higher values result in a more accurate simulation, but increase performance cost. Try to use a low value if possible. |\r\n| Leaf Constraint Iterations \t| The number of leaf segment constraint iterations per frame. Higher values result in a more accurate simulation, but increase performance cost. Try to use a low value if possible. |\r\n| Damping Factor \t| How much of the movement is retained per constraint iteration. Lower values result in a more stiff kelp, whereas higher values result in a more floaty kelp. \t|\r\n| Update Mode \t| The used update mode for the kelp simulation. See Update Mode \t|\r\n| Skip Updates \t| The updates to skip, before the next update is scheduled. See Update Mode \t|\r\nCollision Settings\r\n| Setting \t| Description \t|\r\n|-------------------\t|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\t|\r\n| Enable Collision \t| Should collision be enabled for the kelp? Enabling collision allows the kelp to collide with any collider in the scene, but comes at a performance cost, especially for complex scenes or large amounts of kelp. The collision is calculated per stem segment on the CPU. \t|\r\n| Collision Mask \t| The layermask used for collisions with the environment. \t|\r\n| Segment Collision Radius \t| The radius of the collision sphere per stem segment that is used to approximate the collisions of the kelp stem with its environments. \t|\r\nPerformance Settings\r\n| Setting \t| Description \t|\r\n|--------------------\t|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\t|\r\n| Simulation Distance \t| The distance from the camera at which kelp instances will be simulated. Setting this to a lower value can help with performance. \t|\r\n| Player Transform \t| The transform of the player/main camera. Kelp instances will be simulated based on the player's position. If left empty, the Camera.main will be used. \t|", "wordCount": 597, "readingTime": 3, "isPage": true }, "🖥️ C# API": { "id": "Core-Concepts/C-API", "title": "🖥️ C# API", "order": 4, "content": "<p><img src=\"cachedImage-../images/kelp-renderer-banner.png\" alt=\"\"></p>\n<h1 id=\"C-API\" tabindex=\"-1\">C# API</h1>\n<p>Via the C# API it is possible to add kelp instances. This can be done via the <code>AddKelp</code> method, which takes a position, a height, and a kelp setting.</p>\n<p>Adding kelp can <strong>only be done before the StylizedKelpRenderer has been initialized, which by default happens in <code>OnEnable()</code></strong>.</p>\n<p>Additionally, kelp cannot be removed at runtime.</p>\n<h2 id=\"How-to-add-kelp-in-Awake():\" tabindex=\"-1\">How to add kelp in <code>Awake()</code>:</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-csharp\"><span class=\"hljs-keyword\">public</span> <span class=\"hljs-keyword\">class</span> <span class=\"hljs-title\">KelpSpawner</span> : <span class=\"hljs-title\">MonoBehaviour</span> {\n\n <span class=\"hljs-keyword\">public</span> KelpSettings KelpSettings;\n <span class=\"hljs-keyword\">public</span> StylizedKelpRenderer KelpRenderer;\n\n <span class=\"hljs-function\"><span class=\"hljs-keyword\">void</span> <span class=\"hljs-title\">Awake</span>()</span> {\n KelpRenderer.AddKelp(Vector3.zero, <span class=\"hljs-number\">5</span>, KelpSettings);\n }\n\n}\n</code></pre>\n<h2 id=\"Spawning-kelp-in-a-grid-pattern:\" tabindex=\"-1\">Spawning kelp in a grid pattern:</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-csharp\"><span class=\"hljs-keyword\">public</span> KelpSettings KelpSettings;\n<span class=\"hljs-keyword\">public</span> StylizedKelpRenderer KelpRenderer;\n\n<span class=\"hljs-keyword\">public</span> <span class=\"hljs-built_in\">int</span> gridSizeX = <span class=\"hljs-number\">10</span>;\n<span class=\"hljs-keyword\">public</span> <span class=\"hljs-built_in\">int</span> gridSizeZ = <span class=\"hljs-number\">10</span>;\n\n<span class=\"hljs-function\"><span class=\"hljs-keyword\">void</span> <span class=\"hljs-title\">Awake</span>()</span> {\n KelpRenderer = GetComponent&lt;StylizedKelpRenderer&gt;();\n\n <span class=\"hljs-keyword\">for</span> (<span class=\"hljs-built_in\">int</span> x = <span class=\"hljs-number\">0</span>; x &lt; gridSizeX; x++) {\n <span class=\"hljs-keyword\">for</span> (<span class=\"hljs-built_in\">int</span> z = <span class=\"hljs-number\">0</span>; z &lt; gridSizeZ; z++){\n Vector3 position = <span class=\"hljs-keyword\">new</span> Vector3(x * <span class=\"hljs-number\">2f</span>, <span class=\"hljs-number\">0</span>, z * <span class=\"hljs-number\">2f</span>);\n KelpRenderer.AddKelp(position, Random.Range(<span class=\"hljs-number\">3</span>, <span class=\"hljs-number\">7</span>), KelpSettings);\n }\n }\n}\n</code></pre>\n<h3 id=\"Manually-initializing-the-kelp-renderer:\" tabindex=\"-1\">Manually initializing the kelp renderer:</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-csharp\"><span class=\"hljs-keyword\">public</span> StylizedKelpRenderer KelpRenderer;\n\n<span class=\"hljs-function\"><span class=\"hljs-keyword\">void</span> <span class=\"hljs-title\">Awake</span>()</span> {\n KelpRenderer = GetComponent&lt;StylizedKelpRenderer&gt;();\n KelpRenderer.SelfInitialize = <span class=\"hljs-literal\">false</span>;\n\n <span class=\"hljs-keyword\">for</span> (<span class=\"hljs-built_in\">int</span> x = <span class=\"hljs-number\">0</span>; x &lt; <span class=\"hljs-number\">5</span>; x++) {\n <span class=\"hljs-keyword\">for</span> (<span class=\"hljs-built_in\">int</span> z = <span class=\"hljs-number\">0</span>; z &lt; <span class=\"hljs-number\">5</span>; z++){\n Vector3 position = <span class=\"hljs-keyword\">new</span> Vector3(x * <span class=\"hljs-number\">2f</span>, <span class=\"hljs-number\">0</span>, z * <span class=\"hljs-number\">2f</span>);\n KelpRenderer.AddKelp(position, Random.Range(<span class=\"hljs-number\">3</span>, <span class=\"hljs-number\">7</span>), KelpSettings);\n }\n }\n\n KelpRenderer.Initialize();\n}\n</code></pre>\n<h2 id=\"Adjusting-kelp-renderer-settings-at-runtime\" tabindex=\"-1\">Adjusting kelp renderer settings at runtime</h2>\n<p>The kelp renderer settings themselves can also be adjusted at runtime via script:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-csharp\"><span class=\"hljs-keyword\">public</span> StylizedKelpRenderer KelpRenderer;\n\n<span class=\"hljs-function\"><span class=\"hljs-keyword\">void</span> <span class=\"hljs-title\">Awake</span>()</span> {\n KelpRenderer = GetComponent&lt;StylizedKelpRenderer&gt;();\n\n KelpRenderer.WindStrength = <span class=\"hljs-number\">0.5f</span>;\n KelpRenderer.WindSpeed = <span class=\"hljs-number\">0.2f</span>;\n KelpRenderer.WindScale = <span class=\"hljs-keyword\">new</span> Vector3(<span class=\"hljs-number\">1</span>, <span class=\"hljs-number\">0.5f</span>, <span class=\"hljs-number\">1</span>);\n\n KelpRenderer.SimulationDistance = <span class=\"hljs-number\">25f</span>;\n}\n</code></pre>\n<h2 id=\"Adjusting-kelp-settings-at-runtime\" tabindex=\"-1\">Adjusting kelp settings at runtime</h2>\n<p>The kelp settings can also be adjusted at runtime. This could be used to create a growth effect by increasing the height over time and many more effects:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-csharp\"><span class=\"hljs-keyword\">public</span> KelpSettings KelpSettings;\n\n<span class=\"hljs-function\"><span class=\"hljs-keyword\">void</span> <span class=\"hljs-title\">Update</span>()</span> {\n KelpSettings.LeafWidth += Time.deltaTime;\n}\n</code></pre>\n", "textContent": "C# API\r\n\r\nVia the C# API it is possible to add kelp instances. This can be done via the AddKelp method, which takes a position, a height, and a kelp setting.\r\n\r\nAdding kelp can only be done before the StylizedKelpRenderer has been initialized, which by default happens in OnEnable().\r\n\r\nAdditionally, kelp cannot be removed at runtime.\r\nHow to add kelp in Awake():\r\n\r\n`csharp\r\npublic class KelpSpawner : MonoBehaviour {\r\n\r\n public KelpSettings KelpSettings;\r\n public StylizedKelpRenderer KelpRenderer;\r\n\r\n void Awake() {\r\n KelpRenderer.AddKelp(Vector3.zero, 5, KelpSettings);\r\n }\r\n\r\n}\r\n`\r\nSpawning kelp in a grid pattern:\r\n\r\n`csharp\r\npublic KelpSettings KelpSettings;\r\npublic StylizedKelpRenderer KelpRenderer;\r\n\r\npublic int gridSizeX = 10;\r\npublic int gridSizeZ = 10;\r\n\r\nvoid Awake() {\r\n KelpRenderer = GetComponent();\r\n\r\n for (int x = 0; x ();\r\n KelpRenderer.SelfInitialize = false;\r\n\r\n for (int x = 0; x ();\r\n\r\n KelpRenderer.WindStrength = 0.5f;\r\n KelpRenderer.WindSpeed = 0.2f;\r\n KelpRenderer.WindScale = new Vector3(1, 0.5f, 1);\r\n\r\n KelpRenderer.SimulationDistance = 25f;\r\n}\r\n`\r\nAdjusting kelp settings at runtime\r\n\r\nThe kelp settings can also be adjusted at runtime. This could be used to create a growth effect by increasing the height over time and many more effects:\r\n\r\n`csharp\r\npublic KelpSettings KelpSettings;\r\n\r\nvoid Update() {\r\n KelpSettings.LeafWidth += Time.deltaTime;\r\n}\r\n`", "wordCount": 192, "readingTime": 1, "isPage": true }, "🖼️ How Kelp is Rendered": { "id": "Core-Concepts/How-Kelp-is-Rendered", "title": "🖼️ How Kelp is Rendered", "order": 3, "content": "<p><img src=\"cachedImage-../images/kelp-renderer-banner.png\" alt=\"\"></p>\n<h1 id=\"How-Kelp-is-Rendered\" tabindex=\"-1\">How Kelp is Rendered</h1>\n<p>The kelp is rendered using Unity's Visual Effect Graph (VFX Graph). The VFX Graph allows for highly optimized rendering of large amounts of particles, while also providing a high degree of customization and flexibility. Each particle represents either a stem segment or a leaf.</p>\n<p>In general the kelp uses a rope simulation to simulate the movement of the kelp stem and leaves. This simulation is done mostly on the GPU, using compute shaders and <strong>runs once during FixedUpdate based on the <a href=\"#Performance/Update-Mode\">Update Mode</a></strong>. The kelp stems are simulated on the CPU to allow for collision detection with the environment.</p>\n<p>Per iteration, the following steps are performed:</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Setting</th>\n<th>Where</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Stem Simulation</td>\n<td>GPU</td>\n<td>Simulates the stem segment forces and propagates them within the stem chain.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Stem Constraint &amp; Collision Pass</td>\n<td>CPU</td>\n<td>Constrains the stem segments to ensure they still form a continuous stem without gaps between them. Additionally calculates collision forces that constrain the segments.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Leaf Simulation</td>\n<td>GPU</td>\n<td>Simulates the leaf forces and propagates them within the 3-node chain per leaf.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Leaf Attach-to-Stem Pass</td>\n<td>GPU</td>\n<td>Attaches all leaves to their respective kelp stem segment.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Leaf Constraint Pass</td>\n<td>GPU</td>\n<td>Constrains the leaf nodes to ensure they still form a continuous leaf without gaps between them.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Compute Leaf Points</td>\n<td>GPU</td>\n<td>Computes the individual leaf vertices for each leaf to reduce calculations during rendering.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n", "textContent": "How Kelp is Rendered\r\n\r\nThe kelp is rendered using Unity's Visual Effect Graph (VFX Graph). The VFX Graph allows for highly optimized rendering of large amounts of particles, while also providing a high degree of customization and flexibility. Each particle represents either a stem segment or a leaf.\r\n\r\nIn general the kelp uses a rope simulation to simulate the movement of the kelp stem and leaves. This simulation is done mostly on the GPU, using compute shaders and runs once during FixedUpdate based on the Update Mode. The kelp stems are simulated on the CPU to allow for collision detection with the environment.\r\n\r\nPer iteration, the following steps are performed:\r\n| Setting | Where | Description |\r\n|---------------------------------- |------- |-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\r\n| Stem Simulation | GPU | Simulates the stem segment forces and propagates them within the stem chain. |\r\n| Stem Constraint & Collision Pass | CPU | Constrains the stem segments to ensure they still form a continuous stem without gaps between them. Additionally calculates collision forces that constrain the segments. |\r\n| Leaf Simulation | GPU | Simulates the leaf forces and propagates them within the 3-node chain per leaf. |\r\n| Leaf Attach-to-Stem Pass | GPU | Attaches all leaves to their respective kelp stem segment. |\r\n| Leaf Constraint Pass | GPU | Constrains the leaf nodes to ensure they still form a continuous leaf without gaps between them. |\r\n| Compute Leaf Points | GPU | Computes the individual leaf vertices for each leaf to reduce calculations during rendering. |", "wordCount": 256, "readingTime": 2, "isPage": true } }, "isPage": false, "title": "Core Concepts", "order": 0 }, "FAQs": { "entries": { "❌ Leaves suddenly stop rendering": { "id": "FAQs/Leaves-suddenly-stop-rendering", "title": "❌ Leaves suddenly stop rendering", "order": 2, "content": "<p><img src=\"cachedImage-../images/missing-leaves-banner.png\" alt=\"\"></p>\n<h1 id=\"Leaves-suddenly-stop-rendering\" tabindex=\"-1\">Leaves suddenly stop rendering</h1>\n<p>If your kelp suddenly stops rendering leaves, this usually indicates that the default limit (50k) of the kelp leaf VFX graph has been reached. To increase the default capacity, do the following:</p>\n<ol>\n<li>Open <code>Stylized Kelp &gt; Shaders &gt; Kelp Leaf.vfx</code></li>\n<li>At the top, beneath <code>Initialize Particles</code>, increase the number of particles to, for example, 75,000</li>\n<li>Save the vfx graph and re-enter play mode</li>\n</ol>\n<p>Keep in mind that a lower capacity results in less memory allocation on the GPU. If you notice issues with this, it is recommended to use multiple kelp renderers and disable those that are not visible to the camera.</p>\n", "textContent": "Leaves suddenly stop rendering\r\n\r\nIf your kelp suddenly stops rendering leaves, this usually indicates that the default limit (50k) of the kelp leaf VFX graph has been reached. To increase the default capacity, do the following:\r\n\r\nOpen Stylized Kelp > Shaders > Kelp Leaf.vfx\r\nAt the top, beneath Initialize Particles, increase the number of particles to, for example, 75,000\r\nSave the vfx graph and re-enter play mode\r\n\r\nKeep in mind that a lower capacity results in less memory allocation on the GPU. If you notice issues with this, it is recommended to use multiple kelp renderers and disable those that are not visible to the camera.", "wordCount": 106, "readingTime": 1, "isPage": true }, "🌿 Custom Leaf Texture": { "id": "FAQs/Custom-Leaf-Texture", "title": "🌿 Custom Leaf Texture", "order": 1, "content": "<p><img src=\"cachedImage-../images/main-banner.png\" alt=\"\"></p>\n<p>The leaf texture can be changed on the <code>Stylized Kelp Renderer</code>. Currently, only one leaf texture can be used per kelp renderer.</p>\n<p>To adjust the texture, select the game object with the <code>Stylized Kelp Renderer</code> component and change the <code>Leaf Texture</code> property to your desired texture:</p>\n<p><img src=\"cachedImage-../images/custom-leaf-texture.png\" alt=\"\"></p>\n", "textContent": "\r\n\r\nThe leaf texture can be changed on the Stylized Kelp Renderer. Currently, only one leaf texture can be used per kelp renderer.\r\n\r\nTo adjust the texture, select the game object with the Stylized Kelp Renderer component and change the Leaf Texture property to your desired texture:\r\n\r\n", "wordCount": 46, "readingTime": 1, "isPage": true } }, "isPage": false, "title": "FAQs", "order": 0 }, "Performance": { "entries": { "⚙️ Update Mode": { "id": "Performance/Update-Mode", "title": "⚙️ Update Mode", "order": 2, "content": "<p><img src=\"cachedImage-../images/kelp-renderer-banner.png\" alt=\"\"></p>\n<h1 id=\"Update-Mode\" tabindex=\"-1\">Update Mode</h1>\n<p>The <code>Update Mode</code> property on the <code>Stylized Kelp Renderer</code> component determines how often the kelp simulation is updated. There are three options available:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Fixed Update</strong>: The kelp simulation is updated in the <code>FixedUpdate</code> method. This is the default option and is recommended for most use cases, as it syncs with other physics updates.</li>\n<li><strong>Update</strong>: The kelp simulation is updated in the <code>Update</code> method. This option can be used if you want the kelp to update independently of the physics system for even smoother results.</li>\n<li><strong>Manual</strong>: The kelp simulation is updated manually by calling the <code>Simulate()</code> method. This option gives you full control over when the kelp simulation is updated.</li>\n</ul>\n<p>Additionally, the <code>Skip Updates</code> property can be used to skip a certain number of updates. This can be useful for improving performance, especially if you have a large number of kelp instances in your scene. For example, if you set <code>Skip Updates</code> to 1, the kelp simulation will be updated every other update call based on the <code>Update Mode</code> setting.</p>\n", "textContent": "Update Mode\r\nThe Update Mode property on the Stylized Kelp Renderer component determines how often the kelp simulation is updated. There are three options available:\r\nFixed Update: The kelp simulation is updated in the FixedUpdate method. This is the default option and is recommended for most use cases, as it syncs with other physics updates.\r\nUpdate: The kelp simulation is updated in the Update method. This option can be used if you want the kelp to update independently of the physics system for even smoother results.\r\nManual: The kelp simulation is updated manually by calling the Simulate() method. This option gives you full control over when the kelp simulation is updated.\r\n\r\nAdditionally, the Skip Updates property can be used to skip a certain number of updates. This can be useful for improving performance, especially if you have a large number of kelp instances in your scene. For example, if you set Skip Updates to 1, the kelp simulation will be updated every other update call based on the Update Mode setting.", "wordCount": 171, "readingTime": 1, "isPage": true }, "⚡ Frustum Culling": { "id": "Performance/Frustum-Culling", "title": "⚡ Frustum Culling", "order": 4, "content": "<p><img src=\"cachedImage-../images/kelp-renderer-banner.png\" alt=\"\"></p>\n<h1 id=\"Frustum-Culling\" tabindex=\"-1\">Frustum Culling</h1>\n<p>Frustum culling is a performance optimization technique that involves not rendering objects that are outside the camera's view. Enable this if you notice GPU performance issues due to larger kelp forests. To enable frustum culling for the kelp particle systems, follow these steps:</p>\n<p>Open the <code>Kelp Leaf.vfx</code> &amp; <code>Kelp Stem.vfx</code> graph and click on the <code>Output Particle Mesh (Shader Graph)</code> section at the bottom. In the inspector you should now see the following:</p>\n<p><img src=\"cachedImage-../images/culling-options.png\" alt=\"\"></p>\n<p>Tick <code>Frustum Culling</code> to enable frustum culling. This will ensure that only kelp instances that are within the camera's view frustum are rendered, improving performance.</p>\n", "textContent": "Frustum Culling\r\n\r\nFrustum culling is a performance optimization technique that involves not rendering objects that are outside the camera's view. Enable this if you notice GPU performance issues due to larger kelp forests. To enable frustum culling for the kelp particle systems, follow these steps:\r\n\r\nOpen the Kelp Leaf.vfx & Kelp Stem.vfx graph and click on the Output Particle Mesh (Shader Graph) section at the bottom. In the inspector you should now see the following:\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\nTick Frustum Culling to enable frustum culling. This will ensure that only kelp instances that are within the camera's view frustum are rendered, improving performance.", "wordCount": 100, "readingTime": 1, "isPage": true }, "⚡ General Tips": { "id": "Performance/General-Tips", "title": "⚡ General Tips", "order": 1, "content": "<p><img src=\"cachedImage-../images/kelp-renderer-banner.png\" alt=\"\"></p>\n<h1 id=\"General-Performance-Tips\" tabindex=\"-1\">General Performance Tips</h1>\n<p>The Stylized Kelp asset is designed to be efficient and performant, but there are several ways to optimize its performance further, based on your specific use case.</p>\n<p>In general, consider the following tips:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>\n<p>Use the <code>Simulation Distance</code> property on the <code>Stylized Kelp Renderer</code> to limit the distance at which kelp instances are simulated. This can help reduce the number of kelp instances being simulated at any given time, improving performance.</p>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p>Reduce the <code>Stem Constraint Iterations</code> and <code>Leaf Constraint Iterations</code> properties on the <code>Stylized Kelp Renderer</code>. Lower values result in a less accurate simulation, but can improve performance.</p>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p>If you only have a few kelp instances in your scene, consider reducing the <code>Max Particles</code> property in the <code>Kelp Leaf.vfx</code> &amp; <code>Kelp Stem.vfx</code> graph. This can help reduce memory allocation on the GPU, improving performance. You can view your actual particle count (stem segments, leaf count) used on the <code>Stylized Kelp Renderer</code> component in play mode:</p>\n<p><img src=\"cachedImage-../images/particle-counts.png\" alt=\"\"></p>\n</li>\n</ul>\n<p>Additionally, take a look at the other performance optimization techniques in this section, such as changing the <a href=\"#Performance/Update-Mode\">Update Mode</a>, <a href=\"#Performance/Spatial-Partitioning\">Spatial Partitioning</a>, and <a href=\"#Performance/Frustum-Culling\">Frustum Culling</a>.</p>\n", "textContent": "General Performance Tips\r\n\r\nThe Stylized Kelp asset is designed to be efficient and performant, but there are several ways to optimize its performance further, based on your specific use case.\r\n\r\nIn general, consider the following tips:\r\n\r\nUse the Simulation Distance property on the Stylized Kelp Renderer to limit the distance at which kelp instances are simulated. This can help reduce the number of kelp instances being simulated at any given time, improving performance.\r\n\r\nReduce the Stem Constraint Iterations and Leaf Constraint Iterations properties on the Stylized Kelp Renderer. Lower values result in a less accurate simulation, but can improve performance.\r\n\r\nIf you only have a few kelp instances in your scene, consider reducing the Max Particles property in the Kelp Leaf.vfx & Kelp Stem.vfx graph. This can help reduce memory allocation on the GPU, improving performance. You can view your actual particle count (stem segments, leaf count) used on the Stylized Kelp Renderer component in play mode:\r\n\r\n \r\n\r\nAdditionally, take a look at the other performance optimization techniques in this section, such as changing the Update Mode, Spatial Partitioning, and Frustum Culling.", "wordCount": 181, "readingTime": 1, "isPage": true }, "🌐 Spatial Partitioning": { "id": "Performance/Spatial-Partitioning", "title": "🌐 Spatial Partitioning", "order": 3, "content": "<p><img src=\"cachedImage-../images/kelp-renderer-banner.png\" alt=\"\"></p>\n<h1 id=\"Spatial-Partitioning\" tabindex=\"-1\">Spatial Partitioning</h1>\n<p>Spatial partitioning is a performance optimization technique that involves dividing a large number of objects into smaller groups based on their spatial location. This way you can only activate the kelp renderers in a given area, reducing the number of kelp instances being simulated at any given time and improving performance.</p>\n<p>Key benefits of spatial partitioning include:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Frees up memory on the GPU</li>\n<li>Prevents kelp simulation from running on objects that are not visible to the camera</li>\n<li>Reduces CPU load by skipping physics calculations for kelp instances that are far away from the player</li>\n</ul>\n<h3 id=\"Example-Implementation\" tabindex=\"-1\">Example Implementation</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-csharp\"><span class=\"hljs-keyword\">using</span> System;\n<span class=\"hljs-keyword\">using</span> System.Collections;\n<span class=\"hljs-keyword\">using</span> System.Collections.Generic;\n<span class=\"hljs-keyword\">using</span> Kellojo.StylizedKelp;\n<span class=\"hljs-keyword\">using</span> UnityEngine;\n<span class=\"hljs-keyword\">using</span> UnityEngine.Serialization;\n\n<span class=\"hljs-keyword\">public</span> <span class=\"hljs-keyword\">class</span> <span class=\"hljs-title\">KelpSpatialPartitioner</span> : <span class=\"hljs-title\">MonoBehaviour</span> {\n\n [<span class=\"hljs-meta\">FormerlySerializedAs(<span class=\"hljs-string\">&quot;Player&quot;</span>)</span>] <span class=\"hljs-keyword\">public</span> Transform player;\n <span class=\"hljs-keyword\">private</span> List&lt;StylizedKelpRenderer&gt; _kelpRenderers = <span class=\"hljs-keyword\">new</span> List&lt;StylizedKelpRenderer&gt;();\n\n <span class=\"hljs-function\"><span class=\"hljs-keyword\">private</span> <span class=\"hljs-keyword\">void</span> <span class=\"hljs-title\">Awake</span>()</span> {\n _kelpRenderers.AddRange(FindObjectsByType&lt;StylizedKelpRenderer&gt;(FindObjectsSortMode.None));\n\n <span class=\"hljs-keyword\">var</span> mainCamera = Camera.main;\n <span class=\"hljs-keyword\">if</span> (mainCamera != <span class=\"hljs-literal\">null</span> &amp;&amp; player == <span class=\"hljs-literal\">null</span>) player = mainCamera.transform;\n }\n\n <span class=\"hljs-function\"><span class=\"hljs-keyword\">private</span> <span class=\"hljs-keyword\">void</span> <span class=\"hljs-title\">OnEnable</span>()</span> {\n StartCoroutine(RunPartitioner());\n }\n\n <span class=\"hljs-function\">IEnumerator <span class=\"hljs-title\">RunPartitioner</span>()</span> {\n <span class=\"hljs-keyword\">while</span> (enabled) {\n <span class=\"hljs-function\"><span class=\"hljs-keyword\">yield</span> <span class=\"hljs-keyword\">return</span> <span class=\"hljs-keyword\">new</span> <span class=\"hljs-title\">WaitForSeconds</span>(<span class=\"hljs-params\"><span class=\"hljs-number\">0.5f</span></span>)</span>;\n\n <span class=\"hljs-keyword\">foreach</span> (<span class=\"hljs-keyword\">var</span> kelpRenderer <span class=\"hljs-keyword\">in</span> _kelpRenderers) {\n <span class=\"hljs-keyword\">var</span> distance = Vector3.Distance(kelpRenderer.transform.position, player.position);\n kelpRenderer.gameObject.SetActive(distance &lt; kelpRenderer.simulationDistance);\n }\n }\n }\n\n}\n</code></pre>\n", "textContent": "Spatial Partitioning\r\n\r\nSpatial partitioning is a performance optimization technique that involves dividing a large number of objects into smaller groups based on their spatial location. This way you can only activate the kelp renderers in a given area, reducing the number of kelp instances being simulated at any given time and improving performance.\r\n\r\nKey benefits of spatial partitioning include:\r\n\r\nFrees up memory on the GPU\r\nPrevents kelp simulation from running on objects that are not visible to the camera\r\nReduces CPU load by skipping physics calculations for kelp instances that are far away from the player\r\nExample Implementation\r\n\r\n`csharp\r\nusing System;\r\nusing System.Collections;\r\nusing System.Collections.Generic;\r\nusing Kellojo.StylizedKelp;\r\nusing UnityEngine;\r\nusing UnityEngine.Serialization;\r\n\r\npublic class KelpSpatialPartitioner : MonoBehaviour {\r\n\r\n [FormerlySerializedAs(\"Player\")] public Transform player;\r\n private List _kelpRenderers = new List();\r\n\r\n private void Awake() {\r\n _kelpRenderers.AddRange(FindObjectsByType(FindObjectsSortMode.None));\r\n\r\n var mainCamera = Camera.main;\r\n if (mainCamera != null && player == null) player = mainCamera.transform;\r\n }\r\n\r\n private void OnEnable() {\r\n StartCoroutine(RunPartitioner());\r\n }\r\n\r\n IEnumerator RunPartitioner() {\r\n while (enabled) {\r\n yield return new WaitForSeconds(0.5f);\r\n\r\n foreach (var kelpRenderer in _kelpRenderers) {\r\n var distance = Vector3.Distance(kelpRenderer.transform.position, player.position);\r\n kelpRenderer.gameObject.SetActive(distance < kelpRenderer.simulationDistance);\r\n }\r\n }\r\n }\r\n\r\n}\r\n`", "wordCount": 183, "readingTime": 1, "isPage": true } }, "isPage": false, "title": "Performance", "order": 0 }, "👋 Welcome!": { "id": "Welcome!", "title": "👋 Welcome!", "order": -2, "content": "<p><img src=\"cachedImage-/images/main-banner.png\" alt=\"\"></p>\n<h1 id=\"Welcome!\" tabindex=\"-1\">Welcome!</h1>\n<p>Thank you for purchasing this asset. This means the world to me.</p>\n<p>If you encounter any issues or have questions on how to use the asset for your specific use case, please reach out to me via email (<a href=\"mailto:contact.daniel.fritz@gmail.com\">contact.daniel.fritz@gmail.com</a>), and I'll get things sorted as quickly as possible.</p>\n<p>Additionally, any feature ideas and suggestions are welcome.</p>\n", "textContent": "Welcome!\r\n\r\nThank you for purchasing this asset. This means the world to me.\r\n\r\nIf you encounter any issues or have questions on how to use the asset for your specific use case, please reach out to me via email (contact.daniel.fritz@gmail.com), and I'll get things sorted as quickly as possible.\r\n\r\nAdditionally, any feature ideas and suggestions are welcome.", "wordCount": 57, "readingTime": 1, "isPage": true }, "🚀 Quick Start": { "id": "Quick-Start", "title": "🚀 Quick Start", "order": -1, "content": "<p><img src=\"cachedImage-/images/main-banner.png\" alt=\"\"></p>\n<h1 id=\"Quick-Start\" tabindex=\"-1\">Quick Start</h1>\n<p>Follow the below steps to get started with Stylized Kelp in your project.</p>\n<h2 id=\"Dependencies\" tabindex=\"-1\">Dependencies</h2>\n<p>The asset relies on Unity’s Visual Effect Graph package. To install the package open the Unity Package Manager:</p>\n<ol>\n<li>Navigate to <code>Window &gt; Package Manager</code></li>\n</ol>\n<p><img src=\"cachedImage-/images/open-package-manager.png\" alt=\"\"></p>\n<ol start=\"2\">\n<li>Click the + icon in the top right and select <code>Install package by name...</code></li>\n</ol>\n<p><img src=\"cachedImage-/images/install-by-name.png\" alt=\"\"></p>\n<ol start=\"3\">\n<li>Paste in <code>com.unity.visualeffectgraph</code> and click install</li>\n</ol>\n<p><img src=\"cachedImage-/images/visual-effect-graph.png\" alt=\"\"></p>\n<h2 id=\"Scene-Setup\" tabindex=\"-1\">Scene Setup</h2>\n<ol>\n<li>Add the <code>Stylized Kelp Renderer</code> prefab to your scene, located in <code>Stylized-Kelp &gt; Prefabs</code></li>\n<li>Right click in your hierarchy and pick <code>Create &gt; 3D Object &gt; Stylized Kelp</code></li>\n<li>Click play and see the kelp in action</li>\n</ol>\n<p>From here you can start customizing the kelp to your liking! Check out the <a href=\"#Core-Concepts/Kelp-Settings\">Kelp Settings</a> to get started with customizing the look of your kelp.</p>\n", "textContent": "Quick Start\r\n\r\nFollow the below steps to get started with Stylized Kelp in your project.\r\nDependencies\r\n\r\nThe asset relies on Unity’s Visual Effect Graph package. To install the package open the Unity Package Manager:\r\n\r\nNavigate to Window > Package Manager\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\nClick the + icon in the top right and select Install package by name...\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\nPaste in com.unity.visualeffectgraph and click install\r\nScene Setup\r\n\r\nAdd the Stylized Kelp Renderer prefab to your scene, located in Stylized-Kelp > Prefabs\r\nRight click in your hierarchy and pick Create > 3D Object > Stylized Kelp\r\nClick play and see the kelp in action\r\n\r\nFrom here you can start customizing the kelp to your liking! Check out the Kelp Settings to get started with customizing the look of your kelp.", "wordCount": 124, "readingTime": 1, "isPage": true } }
